questions.explanation: Low displacement (10–15%) underestimates typical hybrid system performance; this would occur only with undersized PV arrays (<3 kW). Moderate savings (USD 1,500–2,500) corresponds to 20–30% displacement, insufficient for the stated 2:1 ratio and full tropical solar resource utilization. Displacement above 50% requires PV oversizing beyond 4:1 ratio or exceptional solar conditions; economically inefficient and not recommended for standard hybrid design. A 10 kW PV array with 5 kW diesel generator achieves 2:1 PV-to-generator ratio (within 2–4 kW PV per 1 kW diesel range). This configuration displaces 30–50% annual diesel consumption (~8,000–12,000 kWh/year from PV generation at 4.0 kWh/m²/day), saving USD 2,000–4,000/year at current diesel costs. System cost approximately USD 25,000–40,000 including battery and hybrid controller. Hybrid solar-diesel systems with 2–4 kW PV per 1 kW generator typically achieve 30–50% annual diesel displacement, generating USD 2,000–4,000 fuel savings annually and improving rural facility sustainability.

questions.rationale: Keep them out of the same raceway or fitting as feeders or branch circuits unless separated or connected as allowed. This matches the checked local source locator for the parent article.
questions.explanation: Transparent glazing achieves only 5–10% efficiency, limiting power density to ~10–20 W/m² despite dual shading function. Solar roof tiles are medium-efficiency products; total power density depends on tile size and spacing, typically lower than vertical facade systems. Thin-film amorphous modules (7–10%) are less efficient than crystalline BIPV options and unsuitable for facade applications. Facade-mounted BIPV systems deliver 100–250 W/m² on vertical surfaces, outperforming transparent glazing (5–10% efficiency yields ~10–20 W/m²) and thin-film modules (7–10% efficiency). Solar roof tiles (50–150 W/tile) are suitable for sloped roofs but less efficient per m² than facade systems. BIPV facade-mounted systems offer superior power density (100–250 W/m²) for vertical building surfaces compared to transparent glazing or thin-film alternatives, making them optimal for commercial building integration.
